$description: The on-open offer to bring a project's `@jxsuite/*` dependencies up to their newest published versions: one sentence, and the packages that would move. A `jx-dialog`, so the platform owns modality, Escape, focus restoration and the backdrop, and the kit draws both answers. Nothing here asks the registry or writes a manifest: `packages/jxsuite-update.ts` keeps the lookup, the dismissal key and the install, and this document only says what is on offer.

style.$description:
The old body was a lit template with no stylesheet at all, which is why the conversion is mostly a deletion. Two `
`s stood in for a paragraph break, and one `` held every package as a single `\n`-joined string — a list spelled as whitespace. Neither is addressable and neither announces as what it is, so a screen reader read one run-on line and a test could only match a substring of it. It is a `
    ` of keyed rows now: the list says how many packages there are, and each row is `[data-package]`. The one token repair travels with it — that span asked for `--spectrum-font-size-75`, which resolves only inside ``, and a document mounted in the dialog layer is outside it, so the size silently fell back to the hard-coded `12px` written beside it.

& [part=\"list\"].$description: Capped and scrolling, because the count is the registry's rather than this dialog's: a project that has not been opened in a year can have every `@jxsuite/*` package behind at once, and a dialog that grows past the viewport puts its own Update button off screen.

& [part=\"package-move\"].$description: Tabular figures, so a column of versions does not jitter between rows of different widths.

children.textContent: Newer versions of these packages have been published. Update the project to them?
